name: Eyelid glue

lead: Eyelid glue is a cosmetic adhesive used to fix the upper lid skin into a fold, producing a temporary double eyelid. The payoff is a visible crease and a larger, more open-looking, defined eye for the day, with no surgery.
It serves the same goal as eyelid tape and is a non-surgical alternative to double eyelid surgery, which creates a permanent crease. No published clinical studies of the glue itself were located.

paras: A thin layer of adhesive holds a fold of lid skin in place so a crease shows when the eye is open. It is applied as part of a daily routine, often with makeup, and lasts until it wears off or is removed.
Any adhesive used next to the eye raises general questions of skin and eye irritation, which have not been specifically studied for these products.

angle.text: Eyelid glue holds the lid skin in a fold to give a visible double eyelid crease and larger, more defined eyes for the day. It is used as a non-surgical alternative to double eyelid surgery. Published research on the product itself is limited.

lead: Eyelid glue, called eye putti (ai puchi) in Japan, is a water-soluble cosmetic adhesive that creates a temporary double eyelid. The glue is painted on the upper lid and the skin is pushed up with a plastic prong and held in a fold, which makes the eyes look bigger and more open and shows more of the lashes [1].

It is used mainly in East Asia, where double eyelids are considered a sign of feminine beauty, and men use it too. Wikipedia says it became available in Japan in the late 1970s, and that the glue needs about a minute to dry and has to be reapplied after a few hours [1]. A variant, eyelid tape or crease tape, is an elastic fibrous strip trimmed to shape and placed on the lid [1].

Eyelid glue is a non-surgical, reversible alternative to double eyelid surgery, which creates a permanent crease [2]. No clinical studies of the glue itself were located; a 2025 study did look at long-term use of double eyelid tape [3].

paras: Wikipedia describes eyelid glue as a water-soluble adhesive that is easy to remove. It is painted on the upper eyelid, the lid is pushed upward with a plastic prong, and the adhesive is left to dry for about a minute so it holds the fold. This creates or deepens a fold that opens the eye and exposes the lashes [1]. Irritation is the only risk Wikipedia mentions [1].

A double eyelid is an upper lid with a visible crease. Wikipedia reports natural prevalence of about 41% among Koreans and roughly 70 to 83% among Chinese and Japanese people, and describes double eyelid surgery as among the most common cosmetic procedures in Taiwan and South Korea. The first recorded operation was performed in Japan in 1896 [2]. Surgical options include non-incisional suture methods, which are quicker but may fade, and incisional methods, which are described as longer-lasting [2]. Temporary products such as glue and tape provide a reversible alternative.
No studies found on eyelid glue.

A 2025 study in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery on double eyelid tape, a related product, surveyed 267 outpatients and measured eyelid laxity, and compared 22 surgery patients with a history of excessive tape use against 11 who never used it. The authors reported higher collagen levels and structural skin changes in tape users, that long-term tape use may cause eyelid laxity and complicate blepharoplasty, and that asymmetry, numbness and hypertrophic scars occurred only in tape users [3].

timeline.event: First recorded double eyelid operation, in Japan [2].
